label: Companies House update · effective 1 December 2026
title: Objecting to a company being struck off: online only from 1 December 2026
summary: If a customer's company owes you money and is about to be struck off, Companies House will stop accepting objections by email from 1 December 2026. Here is how the online service works and what evidence you need.
body:
Companies House announced on 1 September 2026 that it is changing how you object to a limited company being struck off the register. From 1 December 2026, objections must be made through its online service. Companies House says: "We'll no longer accept objections by email after this date."

This matters most if you are owed money. If a customer's company is struck off while it still owes you, getting paid becomes much harder. Objecting in time pauses the strike-off while you take action.

Who can object, and when

  • A shareholder or another interested party, such as a creditor, can object if they have a reason to stop the company being removed, for example a legal claim against it or a debt it owes them.
  • You can only object after notice of the proposed strike-off has been published in The Gazette.
  • You must object before the company is struck off. The Gazette notice gives the strike-off date, which will be either 2 months or 28 days from the date in the notice, so check which applies.

How the online service works

Companies House says it should take around 5 minutes. You will need:

  • A Companies House account (you can create one before you start).
  • The company's name and company number.
  • Supporting documents as images, Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Word or PDF files.

Your documents must:

  • be less than 6 months old;
  • clearly show the company's full name, including the correct ending such as "limited" or "ltd";
  • support your reason for objecting, for example invoices showing the company owes you money;
  • be less than 4MB each.

If you cannot use the online service, or need support because of a disability or health condition, contact Companies House. You may be able to get help using the service, or object by email or post. In that case your objection must arrive at least 2 weeks before the company will be struck off.

What happens after you object

Companies House will tell you whether your objection is successful. If it is, the company will not be struck off for another 6 months. Before that time runs out you need to tell Companies House if you need more time (for example to finish legal action) or if the issue is resolved and you no longer object.

To get more time you must show progress. GOV.UK says sending another invoice is unlikely to be enough, while starting legal action to recover the debt may be accepted. If you do not contact Companies House before the time limit and the company still meets the conditions, it will be struck off.

If the company has already been struck off, the route is a court order to restore it, which is only possible in certain circumstances.

What I would do

If you have unpaid invoices from a limited company customer, look up the company on Companies House now and check whether a strike-off notice has been published. Keep recent invoices and statements in PDF form so you can upload them quickly. If you are a director and want to close your own company, settle what it owes first, because creditors can object and delay the strike-off.
